2.note: Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [Avenge the sons of Israel]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the **vengeance** that he will take on behalf of **the sons of Israel**, not vengeance that they take on their own. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [vengeance on behalf of the sons of Israel]

The expression **you shall be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you will join your people]

Yahweh is referring to Moses dying in a polite way by using the phrase **you shall be gathered to your peoples**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [you shall die]

3.q: הֵחָלְצ֧וּ מֵ⁠אִתְּ⁠כֶ֛ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לַ⁠צָּבָ֑א וְ⁠יִהְיוּ֙ עַל־מִדְיָ֔ן לָ⁠תֵ֥ת נִקְמַת־יְהוָ֖ה בְּ⁠מִדְיָֽן
3.note: Here, **to** marks **give the vengeance of Yahweh on Midian** as the goal or purpose of the command **Equip from with you men for the army**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [in order to carry out Yahweh’s revenge against Midian]

4.note: Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [1,000]

5.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **a thousand for the tribe** before the information about how they **were selected from the thousands of Israel**. Alternate translation: [And a thousand for the tribe were selected from the thousands of Israel]

The expression **were selected** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And the people selected from the thousands of Israel]

6.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe **vessels** that are characterized by their use in **the holy place**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the vessels used in the holy place]

The author is using the possessive form to describe **the trumpets** that were blown to sound **the alarm** in battle. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the trumpets for sounding the alarm]
Here, **hand** represents the charge or care of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in his care]

8.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **they killed** before the information about **Balaam the son of Beor**. Alternate translation: [and they killed Balaam the son of Beor by the sword]

9.note: In this verse, the word **animal** is singular in form, but it refers to all the animals belonging to the Midianites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “animal.” Alternate translation: [their animals]

Here, **strength** represents the wealth and possessions of the Midianites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all their goods]

10.q: וְ⁠אֵ֤ת כָּל־עָרֵי⁠הֶם֙ בְּ⁠מ֣וֹשְׁבֹתָ֔⁠ם וְ⁠אֵ֖ת כָּל־טִֽירֹתָ֑⁠ם שָׂרְפ֖וּ בָּ⁠אֵֽשׁ
10.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **they burned with the fire** before the information about **all their cities with their dwellings and all their encampments**. Alternate translation: [And they burned with the fire all their cities with their dwellings and all their encampments]

The pronoun **their** refers to the Midianites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [all the cities of the Midianites with their dwellings and all the encampments of the Midianites]
The pronoun **they** refers to the Israelite soldiers. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the Israelite soldiers burned with the fire]

11.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the Israelite soldiers who fought against Midian. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the Israelite soldiers took]

In this verse, the word **the man** is singular in form, but it refers to the people they captured as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form. Alternate translation: [among the people]

In this verse, the word **animal** is singular in form, but it refers to the animals the Israelites captured as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “animal.” Alternate translation: [and among the animals]

12.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the Israelite soldiers who fought against Midian. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the Israelite soldiers brought]

13.note: The pronoun **them** refers to the Israelite soldiers returning from the battle. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to meet the Israelite soldiers]

14.note: Here, **strength** represents the fighting force of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the enrolled men of the army]

Moses is using the possessive form to describe **princes** who are characterized by leading **thousands** and **hundreds** of soldiers. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the princes who commanded thousands of soldiers and the princes who commanded hundreds of soldiers]

15.note: Moses is using the question form to rebuke the commanders for sparing the Midianite women. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not have kept every female alive!]

16.note: Moses is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention]
The pronoun **they** refers to the Midianite women whom the soldiers kept alive. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these women]

Here, **word** represents the advice that Balaam gave. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by following what Balaam advised]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **unfaithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to choose to act unfaithfully]

17.note: Moses is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **having known a man to the bed of a male**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [who has slept with a man]

18.note: Moses is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **who have not known a bed of a male**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [who have never had sexual relations with a man]

19.note: Moses is using the adjective **slain** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person, that is, a person who has been killed. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [a person who has been killed]

20.q: וְ⁠כָל־בֶּ֧גֶד וְ⁠כָל־כְּלִי־ע֛וֹר וְ⁠כָל־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה עִזִּ֖ים וְ⁠כָל־כְּלִי־עֵ֑ץ תִּתְחַטָּֽאוּ
20.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **you shall purify** before the information about **every cloth and every vessel of skin and every work of goats and every vessel of wood**. Alternate translation: [And you shall purify every cloth and every vessel of skin and every work of goats and every vessel of wood]

Moses is using the possessive form to describe **work** that is characterized by **goats**, that is, items made from goat hair. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and every item made from goat hair]

23.q: כָּל־דָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־יָבֹ֣א בָ⁠אֵ֗שׁ תַּעֲבִ֤ירוּ בָ⁠אֵשׁ֙ וְ⁠טָהֵ֔ר אַ֕ךְ בְּ⁠מֵ֥י נִדָּ֖ה יִתְחַטָּ֑א וְ⁠כֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יָבֹ֛א בָּ⁠אֵ֖שׁ תַּעֲבִ֥ירוּ בַ⁠מָּֽיִם
23.note: Eleazar uses the word **only** here to indicate a contrast between passing objects through the fire and purifying them with the water of impurity. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [every thing that goes in the fire, you shall pass in the fire, and it will be clean; but it must also be purified in water of impurity. And all that does not go in the fire you shall pass in the water]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **impurity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in water that cleanses what is impure]

The expression **it shall be purified** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you shall purify it]

26.note: Yahweh is using **Lift up the head** as a common expression of the culture to mean “take a count.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Take a count of the spoil of the captive]

27.note: Yahweh is using **the seizers of the battle** as a common expression of the culture to mean the soldiers who fought in the battle. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the soldiers who fought in the battle]

28.note: Here, **life** represents an individual person or animal. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [one individual out of every 500]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [for me]

29.note: Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my contribution]

30.note: Yahweh is using **keeping the keeping** as a common expression of the culture to mean “performing the duties.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones performing the duties of the Dwelling of Yahweh]

32.q: יֶ֣תֶר הַ⁠בָּ֔ז אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּזְז֖וּ עַ֣ם הַ⁠צָּבָ֑א
32.note: This could mean: (1) whatever **plunder** was left after the battle. Alternate translation: [the plunder that the people of the army plundered that was left after the battle] (2) whatever **plunder** was left after each soldier had taken some items for himself. Alternate translation: [the plunder that individual soldiers did not take]

32.q: יֶ֣תֶר הַ⁠בָּ֔ז אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּזְז֖וּ עַ֣ם הַ⁠צָּבָ֑א צֹ֗אן שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֛לֶף וְ⁠שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וַ⁠חֲמֵֽשֶׁת־אֲלָפִֽים
32.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the rest of the plunder that the people of the army plundered was 675,000 flock]

35.note: The author is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and lives of human beings]
See how you translated these same phrases in Numbers 31:18. Alternate translation: [who have never had sexual relations with a man]

36.q: מִסְפַּ֣ר הַ⁠צֹּ֗אן שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֨לֶף֙ וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וְ⁠שִׁבְעַ֥ת אֲלָפִ֖ים וַ⁠חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת
36.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The number of the flock that they received was 337,500]

42.q: וּ⁠מִֽ⁠מַּחֲצִ֖ית בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר֙ חָצָ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִן־הָ⁠אֲנָשִׁ֖ים הַ⁠צֹּבְאִֽים
42.note: This sentence begins here but is interrupted by the list in the following verses and completed in verse 47. If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the half of the sons of Israel** with the information in verse 47 about what Moses took from it. Alternate translation: [And Moses took the following from the half of the sons of Israel, which he divided from the men having fought]

49.note: The soldiers are using **have lifted up the head** as a common expression of the culture to mean “have counted.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [have taken a count of]

The commanders are not referring to a specific **man**. They mean anyone at all. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and not one of us is missing]

50.q: כְלִֽי זָהָב֙ אֶצְעָדָ֣ה וְ⁠צָמִ֔יד טַבַּ֖עַת עָגִ֣יל וְ⁠כוּמָ֑ז
50.note: The phrase **vessel of gold** could be: (1) a general statement that describes each specific ornament. Alternate translation: [—any armlet, bracelet, signet ring, earring, and ornament made out of gold] (2) a specific type of ornament. Alternate translation: [—vessel of gold, armlet, bracelet, signet ring, earring, and ornament]

This could mean: (1) that the commanders realize that God was the one who kept them alive. Because of that, it was as if God owned their lives. They wanted to ransom their lives from God by paying the gold jewelry. Alternate translation: [to redeem our lives from Yahweh] (2) that commanders know that they had sinned or become unclean. They had killed many people. So, they wanted to make sure that God forgave them for what they had done wrong. Alternate translation: [so that Yahweh accepts them and removes our sins] (3) that they had taken a census of the soldiers. It is possible that it was customary to pay a ransom to God after taking a census. [to pay in Yahweh’s presence for each of us who was counted]
Here, **face** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh]

51.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe a **vessel** that is characterized by the **work** that went into making it. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [every skillfully crafted item]

53.note: Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

This could mean: (1) that the soldiers had taken items for themselves, and it was from those items that they dedicated the gold jewelry to Yahweh. Alternate translation: [The gold came from what the men of the army had plundered, a man for himself] (2) that only the commanders of the army dedicated the gold jewelry to Yahweh. The individual soldiers kept what they had **plundered**. Alternate translation: [However, the men of the army kept, a man for himself, what he had plundered]

54.note: This could mean: (1) that Yahweh will remember the Israelites. Alternate translation: [so Yahweh would remember the sons of Israel] (2) that the Israelites will remember what Yahweh did for them. Alternate translation: [where it will be in Yahweh’s presence to remind the Israelites of what had happened]
